title: SafeMCP: Proactive Power Regulation for LLM Agent Defense via Environment-Grounded Look-Ahead Reasoning
evidence: Threat = agent power-seeking from errors/hallucination ('minor errors or hallucinations are magnified into catastrophic failures'); no attacker/adversary in threat model, AgentHarm harmful requests used only as test set. Server-side guard = fine-tuned Qwen3-8B world model (SFT+RL) predicts next state from tool call + partial trajectory/tool results; filters unsafe tools and blocks unsafe calls. Agents: GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Claude-3.5-Sonnet, Gemini-2.0-Flash, Llama-3.1-8B. Over-blocking rate on AgentHarm benign reported (0.01). Cost overhead ~$0.022 (<1.5%).

title: Explainable and Fine-Grained Safeguarding of LLM Multi-Agent Systems via Bi-Level Graph Anomaly Detection
evidence: XG-Guard: unsupervised bi-level (sentence/token) GNN graph anomaly detector on inter-agent dialogue graph, isolates agents by pruning in/out edges. Threats: PI, tool attack (InjecAgent), memory poisoning (PoisonRAG). No adaptive attack ('defender operates strictly at the communication layer'); metrics AUROC/ASR/ACC only; complexity O(NL^2+M) without measured runtime. Backbones GPT-4o-mini, DeepSeek-V3, Qwen3-30B-A3B.

title: SafeAgent: Safeguarding LLM Agents via an Automated Risk Simulator
evidence: Simulator+Evaluator LLM used only to synthesize training data; defense = fine-tuning agent ('internalizes safety constraints ... without imposing latency'), so judge=SELF reading tool observations. Risks incl. 'Environmental Traps ... external triggers (e.g., phishing links) exploit the agent's trust' and user ambiguity. No adaptive attack. Fine-tuned Llama3.1-8B/70B, Qwen2.5-7B, GLM4-9B (closed models only baselines). Data cost ~$0.1 (22k tokens)/scenario; no inference overhead or over-refusal rate. public_bench via ToolEmu (safety benchmark).

title: BlindGuard: Safeguarding LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems under Unknown Attacks
evidence: Adaptive (manual, targets embedding-deviation detection): 'We modify the original PI attack prompt by embedding the correct answer directly into the input and instructing the agent to mimic the reasoning process ... aiming to reduce semantic deviation between malicious responses and normal agent outputs'; AUC stayed high. Unsupervised GAD (SentenceBERT+hierarchical GNN, trained on normal interactions only), bidirectional edge pruning each round. Backbones GPT-4o-mini, DeepSeek-V3, Qwen3-30B-A3B (+Qwen3-8B appendix). Latency 0.53->0.56 min/3 rounds. Attack-free ACC reported; no FPR (AUC only).

title: MCP-Guard: A Multi-Stage Defense-in-Depth Framework for Securing Model Context Protocol in Agentic AI
evidence: Proxy between MCP host and server: Stage I regex/pattern detectors (author-written), Stage II fine-tuned mE5 classifier, Stage III LLM arbiter on raw invocation payload ('[Tool]: {name}; [Args]: {json_params}') only when Stage II ambiguous. Detection-only evaluation on sample datasets, no end-to-end agent backbone (arbiters GPT-4o-mini, DeepSeek-chat, several open models). No adaptive/evasion evaluation. Latency 455.9 ms avg. Precision/recall/F1 reported but no benign block rate.

title: TopoSHIELD: Reshaping the Flow of Malice via Spatio-Temporal Risk-Aware Topological Evolution in Multi-Agent Systems
src: https://aclanthology.org/2026.findings-acl.426/ abstract-only (PDF exceeds fetch size limit; no arXiv version found)
evidence: abstract-only: 'spatio-temporal graph neural network to monitor interaction dynamics, calculating node risk entropy (NRE) and edge attack conductivity (EAC)'; 'pruning high-risk edges and isolating compromised communities to block attack diffusion'; 'reduces toxicity by 58% on GPT-4o while preserving high utility (>90% success rate)'. Adaptive/bench/models not verifiable.

title: The Adaptive Interrogator: Detecting Trojan LLMs in Multi-Agent Systems via Evolved Conversational Strategies
evidence: CTUS: pre-deployment audit; evolutionary algorithm evolves conversational probes, LLM Judge (GPT-3.5/GPT-4/Llama-2-70B) reads suspect agents' responses; per-agent identification only (no removal/isolation described, decisions=flag only). Adversary = supply-chain trojan planter. No trojans designed to evade CTUS. Suspect models Llama-2-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, Gemma-7B, Mistral-7B. FP on fully benign systems (0-2 FP). Convergence iterations 14-105 reported; no tokens/time.

title: ToolSafe: Enhancing Tool Invocation Safety of LLM-based agents via Proactive Step-level Guardrail and Feedback
evidence: TS-Guard (RL-trained guard LLM) judges each tool call before execution over interaction history incl. tool observations; unsafe -> call blocked and guard feedback replaces tool output so agent revises (TS-Flow). Threats MUR, PI, harmful tools, risky args. No adaptive/guard-aware attack. Agents GPT-4o, Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct. Context token overhead +36%/+89%, guard output tokens; detection ACC/F1/Recall only, no explicit FPR.

title: Here Comes the AI Worm: Preventing the Propagation of Adversarial Self-Replicating Prompts Within GenAI Ecosystems
bench: own:Morris-II RAG email worm (Enron emails; Hillary Clinton emails OOD)
evidence: 'we have not tested the resilience of the method against adaptive attacks'. Virtual Donkey: lightweight classifier (logistic regression/NB/decision stump) on BLEU/METEOR/ROUGE-L similarity between GenAI output and retrieved emails, runs after inference; 'alerts the user ... allowing them to review and decide whether to send'. TPR 1.0, FPR 0.015; OOD = unseen payloads/jailbreaks/dataset. Guardrail data from Gemini 1.5 Flash only. 'minimal latency' claimed, not quantified.

title: AirGapAgent: Protecting Privacy-Conscious Conversational Agents
bench: own:synthetic user profiles/contexts with context-hijacking attacks
evidence: Minimizer LLM selects task-relevant user data fields from task+vault only ('the design does not allow any information from the third party to flow back to the minimizer module'). Adversarial third-party app context hijacking; no attack targeting the minimizer/aware of AirGapAgent. Models Gemini Ultra, Gemini Pro, GPT-4, Mistral Large. Utility = share rate of task-relevant fields (over-restriction measured; coded fpr=Y). Request escalation to user only proposed, not evaluated.

title: IsolateGPT: An Execution Isolation Architecture for LLM-Based Systems
evidence: Hub-and-spoke isolation; hub LLM plans from user query+app descriptions, operators deterministically mediate inter-spoke communication; permission prompts for cross-app data/collaboration (hub LLM cross-checks spoke requests against its plan and adds warnings -> judge_exposed Y). Malicious apps threat model; no evaluation of attacks targeting IsolateGPT. GPT-4 only. Latency <30% overhead for 75.73% queries; permission dialog frequency 'appeared for 7.6% on average' (user approval auto-granted in eval).

title: AgentSentinel: An End-to-End and Real-Time Security Defense Framework for Computer-Use Agents
bench: own:BadComputerUse (60 scenarios; tasks from OSWorld/AgentInstruct/AgentBench/NL2Bash + 10 adapted AgentDojo injections)
evidence: Adaptive (manual): 'We analyze the performance of AgentSentinel against five potential adaptive attacks ... Each adaptive attack targets a core component of AgentSentinel'; defends 85% (17/20). Intercepts sensitive OS operations before execution; rule auditor (predefined policies) + LLM auditor correlating task context with system traces. Models Claude 3.5/3.7 Sonnet, GPT-4-Turbo, GPT-4o. FPR 10.8%, task failure 4.2%, ~2.8 security queries per tool use.

title: Towards Automating Data Access Permissions in AI Agents
bench: own:user study permission decisions (203 participants, 7,563 decisions)
evidence: Permission assistant predicts user's allow/deny for data access by a tool/agent: o3-mini in-context learning on user history + LightGCN collaborative filtering; low-confidence escalated to user. Threat: untrustworthy/compromised tools (e.g., via prompt injection) and error-prone LLM. No attack on predictor evaluated. Offline prediction eval, no agent backbone (predictor o3-mini). Acc 85.1%, FPR 15.2%; high-confidence coverage 25.9% (remainder needs user).

title: ACE: A Security Architecture for LLM-Integrated App Systems
bench: InjecAgent (1,054 cases);own:3 new attacks vs IsolateGPT
evidence: Abstract plan from user query only, concrete plan maps to apps (LLM reads app descriptions = schemas), static information-flow check against user-labeled lattice policies, containerized execution isolation; app outputs never enter LLM context. New attacks (execution flow disruption, execution manager hijack, planner manipulation) designed against IsolateGPT, not ACE; no ACE-targeted attack. Models gpt-4o, o3-mini, Claude 3.7 Sonnet, Qwen2.5-72B. Utility 75.2% on InjecAgent; no overhead/FPR.

title: SAGA: A Security Architecture for Governing AI Agentic Systems
bench: own:3 multi-agent tasks (calendar, email, writing);own:8 protocol attacks A1-A8
evidence: Adaptive (manual, protocol-aware): 'We consider 8 adversarial agents that attempt to bypass authentication or access control, including unauthorized connections, token misuse, and contact policy violations'. Provider enforces user-written contact policies, OTKs and access tokens with quotas/expiry; no message-content inspection, no LLM-level/prompt-injection attacks. Models GPT-4.1-mini, GPT-4.1, Qwen-2.5-72B. Overhead <0.61% of task time.
